post.title: US oil is back above $100 a barrel. Here's why
post.ig:
US oil is back above $100 a barrel.
US crude (WTI) settled at $101.41 on Oct 16, 2026, up more than 10% for the week. CNBC tied the jump to attacks on at least 9 ships near the Strait of Hormuz since Oct 11 and a big drop in US crude stockpiles.
Oil flowing through the strait fell to about 70% of its pre-war level (Kpler).
In October 2025, WTI averaged $60.26. US gas averaged $4.33 in September 2026, a record for the month (AAA).
Sources: CNBC, Reuters, Kpler, AAA, World Bank.

US crude oil (WTI) settled at $101.41 a barrel on October 16, 2026, up more than 10% for the week. CNBC tied the move to attacks on at least nine ships near the Strait of Hormuz, while Kpler data showed flows fell to about 70% of pre-war levels. That compares with a $60.26 average in October 2025, and US gas averaged a record $4.33 for September. Sources: CNBC, Reuters, Kpler, AAA, World Bank. News and education, not financial advice.
